[[Euroleague]] | team = '''[[Fenerbahçe Ülker]]''' | number = | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|1992|5|20}} | birth_place = [[Zürich]], [[Switzerland]] | nationality = [[Turkey|Turkish]] | highschool = Stoneridge Preparatory School | college = [[University of Kentucky]] | | draft_team = | draft_year = | career_start = 2008 | career_end = | former_teams = [[Fenerbahçe Ülker]] (2008-2009) | awards = }} '''Enes Kanter''' (born May 20, 1992) is a [[Turkey|Turkish]] [[basketball]] player. A 6-foot-11 [[Center (basketball)|center]], he is currently at the [[University of Kentucky]] serving as a student assistant coach. He was recruited to play for the Wildcats, but the [[NCAA]] declared him permanently ineligible as a collegiate athlete because he received approximately $33,000 from [[Fenerbahçe Ülker]] in excess benefits. The NCAA ruled that this amount was above and beyond what was considered acceptable.[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=5793192 Enes Kanter ruled ineligible][http://news.yahoo.com/s/ap/20101111/ap_on_sp_co_ne/bkc_t25_kentucky_kanter UK center Enes Kanter ruled ineligible by NCAA][http://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/sec/2010-11-11-kentucky-kanter-ineligible_N.htm Kentucky forward Enes Kanter ruled permanently ineligible][http://ncaabasketball.fanhouse.com/2010/11/11/enes-kanter-ruled-ineligible-for-kentucky/ Enes Kanter Ruled Ineligible for Kentucky][http://www.kentucky.com/2010/11/11/1520991/kanter-ruled-ineligible-uk-plans.html#ixzz1534qWRWQ Enes Kanter ruled ineligible; UK plans to appeal] On January 7, 2011, the NCAA rejected Kentucky's appeal, upholding that Kanter is permanently ineligible.[http://www.nytimes.com/2011/01/08/sports/ncaabasketball/08kentucky.html N.C.A.A. Denies Kentucky’s Appeal Over Kanter’s Eligibility] He has declared for the [[2011 NBA Draft]] as a result. ==Early life== Enes Kanter was born May 20, 1992 in [[Zürich]], [[Switzerland]],{{cite newspaper |last=Allen |first=Percy |title=Turkish big man commits to UW basketball team |newspaper=The Seattle Times |date=2009-11-24}} while his father, Mehmet Kanter, attained his [[doctorate]] in [[histology]] from the [[University of Zurich]]. Mehmet Kanter is currently a professor at [[Trakya University]].http://tuh.trakya.edu.tr/html/bolumler/lab/histoloji.htm ==Prep school== Kanter initially tried to enroll at Findley Prep in [[Nevada]] and then at Mountain State in [[West Virginia]], but both attempts were abandoned, reportedly because other schools would not play against a team with Kanter on it. Ultimately, Kanter played for Stoneridge Preparatory School in [[Simi Valley, California]] for the 2009-10 high school basketball season.[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncaa/highschool/news/story?id=4407971&campaign=rss&source=NCBHeadlines Kanter to enroll at Findlay Prep] At the 2010 [[Nike Hoop Summit]], Kanter played for the international team, scoring 34 points and grabbing 13 rebounds. His point total was a record for the event, breaking [[Dirk Nowitzki]]'s record set in the 1998 game. Both [[Rivals.com]] and [[Scout.com]] rated Kanter as a five-star prospect, the highest possible rating.{{cite web |url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/player-Enes-Kanter-102889 |title=Enes Kanter |publisher=Rivals.com |accessdate=2010-04-21}}{{cite web |url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=8&c=1&nid=4508332 |title=Enes Kanter |publisher=Scout.com |accessdate=2010-04-21}} ==College career== On November 23, 2009, Kanter verbally committed to play for the [[University of Washington Huskies]]. Kanter chose Washington over [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] and [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels men's basketball|UNLV]]. However, he re-opened his recruitment in February 2010.{{cite newspaper |title=Kanter commits to Cats Scout.com rates 6-9 forward 5-star prospect |newspaper=Messenger-Inquirer |date=2010-03-24}} On April 14, 2010, Kanter signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play for coach [[John Calipari]] at the [[University of Kentucky]].{{cite web |last=DeCourcy |first=Mike |title=Enes Kanter a revolutionary case for Kentucky, NCAA |publisher=The Sporting News |date=2010-04-14 |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/college-basketball/article/2010-04-14/enes-kanter-revolutionary-case-for-kentucky-ncaa |accessdate=2010-04-21}} ==Professional career== During the 2008-09 season, Kanter was a seldom-used reserve for [[Fenerbahçe Ülker]], a Turkish professional basketball team. He played in at least nine games with the team – four in the [[Euroleague]] and five in the [[Turkish Basketball League]]. Fenerbahçe and [[Olympiacos B.C.]], a [[HEBA A1|Greek League]] basketball team, both offered Kanter professional contracts, but he declined because he wanted to play high school and college basketball in the United States. ==Turkish national team== Kanter was named the Most Valuable Player in the 2009 [[FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]], averaging 18.6 points and 16.4 rebounds while leading Turkey's junior national team to the bronze medal. He declined to play for the senior national team in the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]] which was being held in Turkey and the team would go on to finish 2nd place. His father claimed he did this in order not to miss the first month of classes at Kentucky.[http://aol.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/feed/2010-09/enes-kanter/story/enes-kanters-father-says-turkish-club-is-trying-to-make-an-example-of-his-son Enes Kanter's father says Turkish club is 'trying to make an example' of his son - NCAA Basketball - Sporting News] He wishes to play for the national team in the near future.[http://aol.sportingnews.com/nba/story/2011-05-19/enes-kanter-still-bitter-at-turkish-team-fenerbahce Enes Kanter still bitter at Turkish team Fenerbahce -
